label: late original-phase token from a u/digit/o/c/f/d/n-type set after several x/3/h/l/m/b/y/1/z/v tokens
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, never at t<3, on the delimiter, or during copy. Rate rises with position (orig_idx 3 -> 8: 0.2% -> 9.5%) and with L; activations concentrate in the last few tokens before <DEL>. It mostly fires when the current input is the first occurrence of one of a preferred set (u strongest at 5.7x lift, then 2, 0, o, c, f, d, n, j, a, i), AND the prefix already holds several tokens from a second set (x, 3, h, l, m, b, y, 1, z, v); first_tok x/3/h/l/m/b raises the rate. This looks like a graded, roughly additive read of the token-set content of the hidden state, not a crisp rule. Requiring >=3 prefix tokens from the second set gives dev F1 0.47 and mass recall 0.77; requiring >=4 raises precision to about 0.6 but drops recall. Strongest activations (near max) are on u late in sequences whose prefix is dense in x/3/h/b/m/v. Repeated tokens (in_first=0) rarely fire.
